title: The Locker of Westbrook High
premise: Petra Eastwick has spent four years as Westbrook High's statistician, quietly documenting how the school's legendary football dynasty survives on rigged grades and laundered booster money. When her best friend Marisol vanishes days before the championship that seals Westbrook's centennial glory, leaving only a janitor's keyring in locker 214, Petra discovers Marisol had been building a case against the tradition everyone loves. Following the keys through the school's hidden spaces, Petra must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the town's heart—realizing too late that Marisol never left; she's been hiding inside the school, waiting to see if anyone would come for her. The story ends with Petra testifying at the hearing that dismantles the program, choosing truth over belonging, and walking out of graduation with Marisol at her side.
about_author: Ulyana Okafor is a former high school debate coach who writes stories about the kids nobody puts in the yearbook's front pages. She lives in a small rust-belt town not unlike Westbrook, where she still attends Friday night games and keeps her own statistics.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Opening on game night, Petra runs the stats booth and notices an impossible scoring pattern she's been quietly logging all season. Her only anchor is Marisol, editor of the school paper, who jokes about 'the locker' holding Westbrook's secrets. Emotional beat: weary invisibility, the comfort of counting down days instead of living them.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Marisol misses their Monday ritual, then Tuesday. By Wednesday, police call it a runaway case, but Petra finds locker 214 unlocked with Marisol's notebook gone and a janitor's keyring tagged with seven numbers left behind. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve—the countdown stops mattering.

chapters.title: The Keys Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with flashbacks to Marisol's voice via recovered texts. Petra tests each key: a storage room of decades-old trophies, a boiler tunnel, the principal's archive. Each space reveals the program's rot—altered transcripts, booster slush funds. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into investigation; loyalty to Marisol outweighs fear.

chapters.title: Homecoming Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Coach Danner and Principal Voss gently warn Petra off 'conspiracy thinking,' offering her a college recommendation letter—a bribe dressed as kindness. Her mother, a Westbrook alumna, begs her to let it go. Emotional beat: the town's warmth revealed as pressure; Petra feels the cost of belonging.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (flashback chapters interleaved). Two months earlier: Marisol found the original eligibility files proving star players were academically ineligible, and someone ransacked the paper's office. She hid her evidence in the one place no adult would look. Emotional beat: terror and stubborn courage; readers learn Marisol chose to disappear.

chapters.title: The Seventh Key
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Six keys accounted for; the seventh opens the old field house sub-basement, sealed since the '89 championship. Inside she finds Marisol's evidence cache—and signs someone has been living there recently. A near-collision with a patrolling security guard forces Petra to flee empty-handed except for one photograph. Emotional beat: hope reignited; Marisol may be close.

chapters.title: Friday Night Lights Out
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Championship week. Petra leaks a single altered transcript to a rival paper, forcing Voss to lock down the school—and inadvertently flushing out whoever is hunting Marisol's trail: athletic director Cole Brandt, whose family name is on the stadium. Emotional beat: rising stakes; Petra realizes exposing the truth endangers Marisol if she's still hiding inside.

chapters.title: Sub-Basement
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. During the championship game, while the whole town watches, Petra slips into the sub-basement and finds Marisol, half-starved, who stayed hidden because Brandt threatened her family after she refused to hand over the files. Emotional beat: reunion and rupture—Petra's fury that Marisol didn't trust her, Marisol's shame at being found.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cornered by Brandt in the tunnels beneath the gym, Petra stalls him by reciting his own falsified numbers back at him—her statistician's memory as a weapon—while Marisol livestreams the confrontation from the vents. The recording goes viral before halftime ends. Emotional beat: climax; invisible skills become visible power.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Weeks later: the state investigation dissolves the program, Brandt is indicted, and the town grieves its myth even as it begins to heal. At graduation, Petra crosses the stage not as a footnote but as herself, Marisol cheering from the stands. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—truth cost them the town's love but gave them each other and themselves.
